name: The UAT Dashboard Maker
oneLiner: Parses the returned UAT spreadsheet — even a wide-format sheet several testers filled side by side — and emits a one-slide dashboard, an HTML page, and raw JSON with the go/no-go call computed.
lead: The last gate before launch is UAT: real users exercise the app and log pass/fail plus comments into an `.xlsx` workbook. This agent parses that workbook — detecting when multiple testers shared one sheet in wide format — aggregates pass/fail counts, classifies failures into buckets, computes coverage and pass rate, evaluates them against exit criteria, and renders a single PowerPoint slide plus a self-contained HTML dashboard showing coverage, pass rate, the issue list, and launch readiness.
chore: The manual path: open the returned workbook, count prompts tried, passed, and failed, bucket the failures, compute the pass rate, check it against exit criteria, then hand-build a summary slide for the go/no-go meeting. Error-prone counting plus hours of slide work, redone every time a fresh workbook comes back.
instead: Point the agent at the workbook (or the folder it lands in) and get back a finished dashboard slide, a matching HTML page, and the raw JSON — counting, classification, and exit-criteria evaluation all done.
whyItMatters: The go/no-go launch decision rests on these numbers, so counting them correctly and rendering them unambiguously is exactly what a room of decision-makers needs.

howItWorks.step: Resolves the input path: a file is used directly; a directory is scanned for `.xlsx` files (skipping `~$` temp locks and dotfiles) and the newest by mtime is picked.
howItWorks.explain: Accepts **either a file or a drop-folder** so testers can dump workbooks somewhere shared without renaming anything. The `~$` filter is the load-bearing quirk — Excel writes a `~$whatever.xlsx` **lock file whenever a workbook is open in the app**, and handing that placeholder to the parser throws, so it's excluded alongside dotfiles. When a directory is given it picks the **newest by `mtimeMs`** (filenames aren't reliably sortable), and both the missing-path and empty-folder cases `process.exit(1)` — a **hard fail is preferred over silently parsing nothing** and emitting a bogus dashboard.

howItWorks.step: Auto-detects single- vs. multi-tester layout by matching repeating `Tester #N: Name` headers in the sheet's second row.
howItWorks.explain: Layout detection is **data-driven, not configured** — it reads row 2 (the note row) and counts how many cells match a `Tester #N: Name` banner. The regex is deliberately **forgiving** (`#` optional, flexible whitespace, case-insensitive) because testers hand-type those headers inconsistently, and `String(row2[c] || '')` coerces numeric/empty/`undefined` cells so `.match` never throws. The **`> 1` threshold is the real decision**: one banner (or none) is a normal single-tester sheet and returns `null`, while two or more means a shared wide-format workbook whose `colOffset`s tell the parser where each tester's column block begins. A blank name after the colon **falls back to `Tester #N`** so no block is left unlabeled.

howItWorks.step: Aggregates pass/fail across the Sample Prompts and New Prompts sheets, computes coverage and combined pass rate, and evaluates each exit criterion (coverage, pass rate ≥ 80%, zero high-severity issues, formal sign-off).
howItWorks.explain: Counts key off the **exact strings `'Pass'`/`'Fail'`**, so blank or untested rows fall through both filters and never inflate either tally — deliberate, since an unanswered prompt is neither a pass nor a fail. `passRate` guards divide-by-zero so an all-untested round reports **`0`, not `NaN`**. `testCoverage` is a **Set comparison** (`passedTestNums.size >= uniqueTestNums.size`): a prompt passed by any one of several testers counts once, and coverage is met only when every distinct test number has at least one pass. The exit bar is **fixed and strict** — `passRate >= 80`, `highIssues === 0` (zero, not 'few') — and `formalSignOff` is **hardcoded `false`** so the numbers can never auto-satisfy what is a human sign-off.

howItWorks.step: Classifies each failed result into a named bucket, retaining feature area, classification, and the tester's comment (falling back to the actual result when no comment was left).
howItWorks.explain: A pure **shape-narrowing map** — no filtering, so every failed result becomes exactly one issue record and nothing is dropped. The two `||` cascades are the real logic: `classification` falls back through the tester's explicit bucket, then the **feature area as a coarse bucket**, then `'Other'`, guaranteeing no failure is left uncategorized on the dashboard. `comment` prefers the tester's own note but **falls back to the machine-observed `actualResults`** when they left the comment blank, and finally a `'(no comment)'` placeholder so the rendered issue row never shows an empty cell.

howItWorks.step: Renders a one-slide `LAYOUT_WIDE` PowerPoint via `pptxgenjs` — header bar, coverage/pass-rate rings, metric cards, and issue bars — plus a matching HTML dashboard and a JSON dump, unless `--dry-run` was passed.
howItWorks.explain: `pptxgenjs` is pulled in via **dynamic `import()`**, not a top-level require, so a `--dry-run` (which never calls this function) doesn't pay to load the heavy slide library. `LAYOUT_WIDE` fixes the canvas at **13.33×7.5in — 16:9**, the projector ratio for the go/no-go meeting, and every coordinate thereafter is in **inches**, with `w: '100%'` spanning the header band the full slide width. The title uses a **single `addText` with two runs** so the bold 'UAT Summary' and the lighter date sit on one baseline in one text box rather than two overlapping shapes. The whole function is `async` and `writeFile` is awaited so the caller is guaranteed the `.pptx` is **fully flushed to disk** before it moves on to the HTML and JSON deliverables.

examples.caption: Three testers, one wide-format workbook
examples.input: A workbook where three testers each filled their own column block against the same prompt list.
examples.output: `detectWideFormat()` resolves three tester blocks, their results combine into one pass rate, and coverage plus issues render across all three on a single slide.

examples.caption: Dry-run before writing files
examples.output: A plain-text summary to stdout — coverage, pass rate, issue counts, and each exit criterion marked met/not — with no `.pptx`, `.html`, or `.json` written.

examples.caption: Exit criteria clear the bar
examples.input: A completed round at 84% pass rate, every prompt passed by at least one tester, and zero high-severity issues.
examples.output: A dashboard with green rings, the first three exit criteria marked met, and the fourth — `formalSignOff` — marked pending, since that boolean is hardcoded to a human decision.

underHood.heading: Resolve the workbook
underHood.whenRuns: First, on the input path you pass.
underHood.input: A file path, or a directory where testers drop filled-in workbooks.
underHood.output: One resolved `.xlsx` path — the newest by mtime when a directory is given (via `resolveInputFile()`).

underHood.heading: Parse the workbook
underHood.whenRuns: Immediately after the file is resolved.
underHood.input: The 'Sample Prompts', 'New Prompts', and 'Testers' sheets in the workbook.
underHood.output: Every row parsed into structured records via the `xlsx` library.

underHood.heading: Detect tester layout
underHood.input: The header row and the row below it.
underHood.output: Either a single-tester layout, or — via repeating `Tester #N` column blocks every six columns — a multi-tester layout with each tester's columns mapped correctly (via `detectWideFormat()`).

underHood.heading: Aggregate metrics
underHood.whenRuns: After every row from every sheet is parsed.
underHood.input: The full list of per-test results — pass, fail, or untested — across all testers.
underHood.output: Coverage, pass/fail counts, and pass rate for the Sample and New prompt sheets, combined into one set of totals (via `aggregateMetrics()`).

underHood.heading: Classify failures and evaluate exit criteria
underHood.input: Every failed result and its comment.
underHood.output: Issue counts per named bucket, plus a met/not-met/pending evaluation of the four exit criteria: coverage, pass rate ≥ 80%, zero high-severity issues, and formal sign-off (via `classifyIssues()`).

underHood.heading: Render the deliverables
underHood.output: A one-slide PowerPoint (ring and bar charts via `pptxgenjs`), a matching self-contained HTML dashboard, and a JSON dump of every number, ready for the go/no-go meeting (via `generatePptx()`).

prerequisites: Node ≥ 18 and a terminal (macOS/Linux shell or Windows PowerShell).
The filled-in UAT workbook (the final round where real users exercise the app before launch) as an `.xlsx` file, or a directory where those get dropped.

steps.label: Install Node.js — the runtime for the agent.
steps.cmd:
# macOS (with Homebrew):
brew install node

# or download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, then check it worked:
node -v   # should print v18 or higher
steps.why: The agent is a TypeScript program; Node executes it. One-time per machine.
steps.firstRun: Needed only the first time on a new machine.

steps.label: Clone the agents and install dependencies.
steps.why: `npm install` pulls the agent's dependencies — `xlsx` for parsing and `pptxgenjs` for the slide — into `node_modules`.
steps.rerun: No-op unless the dependency list changed.

steps.label: No env vars needed — just know where the workbook lives.
steps.cmd:
# example: a single returned workbook
./returned-uat-results.xlsx

# or a shared folder several testers dropped their copies into
./uat-results/
steps.why: Unlike agents that hit a work board or an LLM, this one only reads a local `.xlsx` — there's nothing else to configure.

steps.label: Dry-run first, writing no files.
steps.why: `--dry-run` prints the aggregated numbers — coverage, pass rate, issues, exit criteria — to stdout, so you can verify the sheet parsed correctly before rendering the slide.

steps.label: Run for real and open the dashboard.
steps.why: Without `--dry-run`, it writes all three deliverables: a one-slide PowerPoint with ring and bar charts, a self-contained HTML page, and the raw JSON — ready to drop into the go/no-go meeting.
steps.firstRun: Parses every row, detects the tester layout, and builds all three files fresh.
steps.rerun: Point `--input` at the folder instead of one file and it always picks the newest `.xlsx` by mtime — handy once a newer round of results comes back.

inputs.name: --input <path>
inputs.desc: A single `.xlsx` workbook, or a directory — in which case the newest `.xlsx` by mtime is used.

inputs.name: --dry-run
inputs.desc: Print the aggregated summary to stdout only; skip writing the `.pptx`, `.html`, and `.json`.

outputs.name: UAT_Dashboard_<timestamp>.pptx
outputs.desc: A one-slide PowerPoint with coverage and pass-rate ring charts, issue bar charts, and the four exit-criteria checks.

outputs.name: UAT_Dashboard_<timestamp>.html
outputs.desc: A self-contained HTML dashboard of the same metrics, shareable without opening PowerPoint.

outputs.name: UAT_Dashboard_<timestamp>.json
outputs.desc: Every aggregated number in raw form — coverage, pass rate, issues by bucket, and the exit-criteria checklist.

runbook.rerun: Re-run whenever a fresh workbook comes back from a new tester round — point `--input` at the shared drop folder and it always picks the newest file by mtime, so the dashboard never goes stale. Nothing needs clearing between runs; each writes a new timestamped set of files.
runbook.integrate: Drop the completed workbook into the shared folder as the last step of a UAT round, then run this agent as the trigger for the go/no-go meeting — the `.pptx` is what gets projected, the `.json` is what gets archived alongside the decision.

video.caption: 2-min screen recording: point the agent at a filled-in UAT `.xlsx` and watch the dashboard slide render.
script: Open a terminal next to the returned UAT spreadsheet so viewers see both.
Say: 'This agent turns the messy spreadsheet real users fill in during their final try-out into one clean dashboard slide.'
Open the spreadsheet briefly — show the Pass/Fail column and a tester's comment on a failed row.
Run `node -v` to confirm Node is installed; say one line about what Node is.
Run `npm install` (or note it's already done); explain it's grabbing the spreadsheet-reading and slide-building libraries.
Run the `--dry-run` command; point out the printed coverage, pass rate, and exit-criteria lines in the terminal.
Run the same command without `--dry-run`; narrate that it's now writing the actual slide and web page.
Open the `.pptx`; point at the coverage ring, the pass-rate ring, and the issue bar chart.
Point out the fourth exit criterion — formal sign-off — always shown as pending, since that's a human decision.
Close: 'The go/no-go call rests on these numbers — this is what a room full of decision-makers actually needs.'
